cohort: 84 singleton pregnancies with antenatally diagnosed vasa previa and no fetal anomalies
finding: Asymptomatic women with an antenatal diagnosis of vasa previa, singleton pregnancies, and at low risk for preterm birth may be safely managed as outpatients, as long as they are able to access hospital promptly in the event of antepartum bleeding or early labor.
mod_finding: Unplanned cesarean deliveries were highest in the symptomatic hospitalized group (40%) compared to the asymptomatic hospitalized (0%) and outpatient (13.3%) groups.
